title: Atmospheric Dynamics
tagline: Atmospheric thermodynamics, radiative transfer, cloud physics, equations of motion on a rotating planet, balanced flow, vorticity, the boundary layer and the general circulation
summary: This course turns the physics behind the weather into equations. It covers the thermodynamics of dry and moist air, radiative transfer, cloud physics, the equations of motion on a rotating planet, geostrophic and thermal-wind balance, vorticity and Rossby waves, the turbulent boundary layer, and baroclinic instability and the general circulation of the atmosphere.

chapters.title: Atmospheric thermodynamics
chapters.summary: The gas laws, the first law of thermodynamics for air parcels, potential temperature and hydrostatic balance.

chapters.title: Moist thermodynamics
chapters.summary: The Clausius–Clapeyron relation, equivalent potential temperature, thermodynamic diagrams and convective available potential energy.

chapters.title: Radiative transfer
chapters.summary: Absorption, emission and scattering by gases, aerosols and clouds, and the radiative heating and cooling of the atmosphere.

chapters.title: Cloud physics
chapters.summary: Nucleation, droplet growth by condensation and collision, ice processes and the formation of precipitation.

chapters.title: Equations of motion on a rotating Earth
chapters.summary: Forces on air parcels, the Coriolis force, scale analysis and the primitive equations.

chapters.title: Balanced flow
chapters.summary: Geostrophic, gradient and thermal winds, and the effects of friction.

chapters.title: Vorticity and Rossby waves
chapters.summary: Circulation, vorticity, potential vorticity and planetary Rossby waves.

chapters.title: The atmospheric boundary layer
chapters.summary: Turbulence, the surface fluxes of heat, moisture and momentum, and the daily cycle of the boundary layer.

chapters.title: Baroclinic instability and the general circulation
chapters.summary: Hadley cells, jet streams and mid-latitude eddies, and how the atmosphere transports heat and momentum.
